clue.text: Part support-but not for long

parts.note: to part is to split, as a crowd or a path divides
to second a motion is to support it

explanation.surface: Someone offers to back a proposal, but only briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjectival phrase: a split-second decision is one that takes no time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A split second is a fraction of a moment, so something lasting that long is very brief.

clue.text: Getting solid framework

definitions.meaning: as jelly or concrete hardens it is said to be ...
the mount or frame that holds a jewel, or the backdrop of a story

explanation.surface: A builder describes concrete hardening into a sturdy frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday: concrete firming up, and the mount that frames a gem or scene.

clue.text: It's not good in the French town

indicators.note: the word for poor health goes inside the French article

parts.note: LE is the French masculine word for 'the'
ill means unwell or poor, not good

explanation.surface: Something unpleasant is going on in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' is only a link; the French article wraps around the word for poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lille is a large town in northern France near the Belgian border.

clue.text: Bullies, and then tears result

indicators.note: the letters of the two words produce, as a result, a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Victims of a bully end up crying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bullies' is a verb here, third person: it intimidates.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully someone is to intimidate them, much as one menaces with harm.

clue.text: An island some people feel badly about

indicators.note: only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lying within them

explanation.surface: An island that certain people resent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes a run from feEL BAdly; 'about' is a link. Napoleon, exiled there, perhaps felt badly about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is the Mediterranean island off Tuscany where Napoleon was first exiled.

clue.text: Foreign love poetry has a point

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, shaped like the letter O
verse is another word for poetry
S, south, is one of the points of the compass

explanation.surface: Romantic verse from abroad makes a sharp argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' is a compass point here, not a tip or argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas means from or in another country, abroad.

clue.text: A little drink may be taken before a show

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: Theatregoers have a quick nip before the performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be taken before' tells you DRAM comes before A.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play, a show put on stage.

clue.text: Stuff for tea isn't cooked

indicators.note: cooked means altered or falsified, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A complaint that the tea is not properly made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' means fabric, not food or things.
explanation.definitionFit: Satinet is a thin imitation satin, a kind of cloth or stuff.

clue.text: Declare, not for the first time, soldiers need a lock-up

definitions.text: Declare, not for the first time

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of British soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for a lock is read from the bottom

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Soldiers insist again that they need a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock-up' looks like a prison, but splits into a lock of hair and 'up', which in a down answer turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassert is to state or claim something once more.

clue.text: It's only fair the board should accept new role

indicators.note: the board takes in the other letters, holding them inside itself

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

indicators.note: new signals the letters of role made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A committee agrees it is reasonable to take on a fresh position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' turns ROLE into OLER, which TABLE accepts: T-OLER-ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerable means passable or middling, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Time taken by conservationists' representative

indicators.note: the word for time is followed and claimed by the conservation body

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
NT is the National Trust, Britain's heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Conservation group's spokesperson is a time-waster.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Trust (NT) looks after historic British buildings and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent acts on someone else's behalf, as a representative does.

clue.text: The great height's topping!

parts.note: reads as praise of a lofty view but means the frozen covering on top of a high mountain

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the lofty view is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' sounds like old-fashioned British praise, but it literally means what tops the peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A permanent covering of ice sits on high summits and the poles.

clue.text: Criminal finding dope doubly favoured

indicators.note: the word for a fool is used twice over

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
in favour, popular, is in

explanation.surface: A crook found to be twice as stupid yet popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'favoured' gives IN, as in 'in favour'.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, a criminal who kills for hire or politics.

clue.text: There's danger in concocting such a plot

indicators.note: concocting means making something up, so the letters are mixed afresh

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Hatching such a scheme is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' is a patch of land, not a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden is a cultivated patch of land beside a house.

clue.text: Carried out, being plastered

definitions.meaning: a service ... is one performed or carried out
a wall is ... when coated with plaster or cement

explanation.surface: A drunk is carried out of the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' looks like drunk, but it is coated with render.
explanation.definitionFit: Render means both to perform a service and to coat a wall with cement.

clue.text: Financial record agreed with a woman in a huff

indicators.note: the agreement and the woman go inside the word for a sulk

parts.note: in a pet means in a huff, a fit of pique
ay is an old word for yes, agreed
she stands for any woman

explanation.surface: A woman agrees to the accounts while sulking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a huff' is PET, as in 'in a pet': P-AY SHE-ET.
explanation.definitionFit: A paysheet lists wages paid, a record kept for accounting.

clue.text: Consumers could well be twisters!

parts.note: eaters twirl long thin pasta strands on a fork, so they could be called twisters

explanation.surface: Shoppers might be swindlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisters' suggests cheats or tornadoes, but diners twist this pasta around a fork.
explanation.definitionFit: Long strands of Italian pasta are eaten by winding them on a fork.

clue.text: Arrangements for defence-revolutionary, but so cunning

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist revolutionary

indicators.note: cunning means artful or crafty, so these letters are artfully rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Defensive plans by a crafty rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunning' turns BUT SO into OUBTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Redoubts are small fortifications built to defend a position.

clue.text: The 10 an underground worker set about first

indicators.note: the miner is placed around the abbreviation for first

parts.note: a miner works underground in a pit
1st, first, is written IST

explanation.surface: A pit worker took the lead first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The 10' points to 10-across, AGENT: a minister acts for a king or state.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister acts on behalf of a government or sovereign, as an agent does.

clue.text: Note a home is shabby in the extreme

parts.note: me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a nest is a bird's home

explanation.surface: A sad note that a home is very run-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean means shabby or poor, so the superlative is the shabbiest of all.

clue.text: Guy has invested money in a lake

indicators.note: the sign for money goes into the word for a lake

parts.note: a lake is a body of water
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for a pound

explanation.surface: A man has sunk his savings in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is just a man; WATER takes in L: WA-L-TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter is a man's first name, and a guy is any man.

clue.text: Like a queen totally dressed in grey perhaps

indicators.note: the word for totally is clothed by the other letters
perhaps suggests a possible variant, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
all means totally, wholly

explanation.surface: A queen dressed completely in grey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns GREY into REGY, which takes in ALL: REG-ALL-Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Regally means in a royal manner, befitting a monarch.

clue.text: A form of hostility

parts.note: a version is a form or variant of something

explanation.surface: Antagonism takes many shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion is a strong dislike, close to enmity.

clue.text: Surreptitiously move left within the party

indicators.note: the abbreviation for left sits inside the word for a party

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute or game

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks off leaving a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' is a side in a dispute, not a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to edge along furtively.

clue.text: Strip without the right for the press

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the strip goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: a thong is a thin strip of leather
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Undressing without permission for the journalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in the old sense 'outside'; 'press' is a crowd, not newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A press is a dense crowd of people, a crush.

clue.text: Unavailable to a trainee? Rubbish!

parts.note: a dish that is off the menu is unavailable
L, for learner, marks a trainee driver

explanation.surface: Something forbidden to a learner is dismissed as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails of a slaughtered animal, so also refuse or rubbish.

clue.text: Decree a quarter must be green

parts.note: a law is a decree
N, north, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An order that one district must go green.
explanation.definitionFit: A green is a stretch of mown grass, as a lawn is.

clue.text: In certain sports little men do better

indicators.note: sports means displays or wears, so the words show the answer within them

explanation.surface: In some games small players improve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here, improve; the run is littlE MEN Do.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct or improve a text.

clue.text: Familiar acts are through love" (Prometheus Unbound Shelley)

definitions.text: Familiar acts are through love" (Prometheus Unbound Shelley)

parts.words: Familiar acts are through love" (Prometheus Unbound Shelley)
parts.note: a quotation from Shelley's poem with one word missing before 'through love'

explanation.surface: A line from Shelley's verse drama.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line reads 'Familiar acts are ___ through love', so supply the missing adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelley's line says ordinary deeds become lovely when done in love.

clue.text: Basically altering a style's line

indicators.note: altering means changing, so these letters are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Fundamentally, changing a fashion's cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentially means fundamentally, at root.
